mostWorthwhile.text: Following fat from intestinal cells into chylomicrons and then lymph was most worthwhile: it distinguished fat’s route from the blood route taken by glucose and amino acids.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate glucose and amino-acid crossings were clear but repetitive; both planned pictures showed the same cell-to-capillary route without explaining the transport mechanisms.

surprise.text: Inspecting glucose automatically combined it with amino acids to show their shared portal-blood route. The result described blood travelling to the liver, though it did not explain the term “portal.”

arbitrary.text: Directly combining fat with the packaging materials and then chylomicrons with the lacteal entrance seemed physically plausible, but both required the villus as a station. Compatibility feedback completed each operation, though the station requirement was not obvious.

continue.text: I would continue: comparing nutrient routes was useful, and I would be curious to see what happens at the liver. The repeated station requirement made some choices less intuitive, however.
